text:
alex: Recap from today's dedicated GPU orchestration sync. Proposal: use short 'stabilize windows' plus per-tenant 'burst vouchers' (micro + long) to smooth autoscale churn. Sketch below.

mika: lifecycle in 3 bullets please.

alex: 1) tenant requests burst -> consume voucher if available and headroom exists; 2) controller emits scale-intent and opens stabilize_window (base 60s); 3) nodes for that intent are protected from immediate delete/evict until window end; if demand falls we keep nodes until expiry and drain pods.

toby: protecting nodes helps, but will that blow past cluster capacity when many tenants burst?

alex: guardrail: global_burst_headroom_pct (default 12%). If admitted headroom > governor, new bursts are rejected with 429 soft-reject plus suggested backoff. Governor reduces as utilization rises.
rina: vouchers how replenish? daily vs weekly?

mika: split pool: micro_vouchers refill daily (small amount), long_vouchers allocated weekly from committed allotment. Micro handles transient spikes.
sam: how do we deter noisy tenants that pulse continuously?

alex: penalty curve: voucher_cost *= (1 + alpha * consecutive_spikes) within a short window. Also consecutive_spike_count metric for audit and throttling.

lee: what about eviction suppression risk? if those nodes are full of warm pods but other tenants need capacity?

alex: suppression only applies to nodes created for the intent and only for the stabilize_window. Preemption still applies to reclaim preemptible slices. If cluster becomes constrained, admissions stop.

mika: adaptive window idea? static 60s might not fit all clouds.

alex: yes: stabilize_window = clamp(30s, 120s, p95_provision_latency * 1.15). Controller computes p95 from recent telemetry.
toby: fallback when we can't provision? route to smaller quantized model variant, then cross-region if policy allows, then queue with TTL.
rina: queue semantics? 202 vs 429?

alex: if queued return 202 + Retry-After with estimated ETA. If queue TTL expires refund the voucher and return 503. We also emit refund events for billing.
sam: metrics to add?

alex: add: burst_voucher_balance{tenant}, burst_admit_total, consecutive_spike_count{tenant}, stabilize_window_seconds, scale_intent_pending_seconds, p95_provision_latency.

lee: operator config example for infra to implement? short YAML please.

alex: ```yaml
apiVersion: redwood.io/v1
kind: PoolAutoscalePolicy
spec:
  baseStabilizeWindowSec: 60
  adaptiveMultiplierP95: 1.15
  vouchers:
    microDaily: 40
    longWeekly: 200
    penaltyAlpha: 1.25
  globalBurstHeadroomPct: 12
  queueTTLsec: 300
```

mika: rollout plan? we need sim traces and metric gates.

alex: plan: sim harness replaying 30 days of traces in staging (2w), staging canary (1w), 3-customer pilot on dedicated-test (3w), feature-flagged rollout with metric gates (node-churn, pct-429, median-tail-latency).

toby: please include a cost delta calc for sales so they can estimate bill impact of micro vs long vouchers.

alex: will add simple model in the PR (voucher burn rate -> expected extra node-minutes).

ops-bot: RFC updated -> https://redwood.rfc/internal/surge-stabilizer-v1

rina: add support playbook for queued refunds and troubleshooting steps.

mika: agreed. I'll open a short RFC follow-up + PR with sim plan and example dashboards.

alex: thanks all. I'll file PR and ping reviewers.
